attach_section.replacement:
**Attach semantics.** The default `cache_scope="process"` keeps process-lifetime
attachment: the last process attachment is used by bare inference after warmup.
`cache_scope="context"` instead resolves and hydrates the selected managed identity
without ever changing that process pointer. The framework must select the same
identity while tuning and during capture-time forward warmups and capture. Full
captured replay repeats no Python lookup. Eager tails remain outside the graph scope.
Scoped identities exclude legacy-loaded and bundled configs, leaving legacy serving
state intact. Store objects and their memos remain registered across scope exits.
Nested v2 contexts are still unsupported; nesting ordinary `autotune()` is unchanged.
Concurrent tuning/serving, distributed scoped-store use and scoped reload remain
outside this initial qualification.

mixed_execution_section.replacement:
**Mixed execution policies.** Actual framework execution and capture coverage determine the
policy; eager and graph buckets are not necessarily disjoint. An optional
`autotune_v2(..., cache_scope="context")` selects a managed identity for a bounded region
without changing the ambient store. The framework must tune covered profiles before capture
and use the same identity for capture-time lookup; full graph replay performs no Python lookup.
Eager tails stay outside that scope. Identified scopes do not inherit untagged legacy or bundled
configs. `cache_scope="process"` retains existing attachment and lookup behavior by default.
This does not change the process-global tuning-mode counter: concurrent tuning and serving
are not qualified by scoped attachment. Nested v2 contexts remain unsupported. Identified
scoped tuning rejects `rank_tactics(k>1)` until its winner writes honor the selected identity.
`autotune_v2_reload()` inside a context scope is unsupported; outside it still targets the
ambient store. Distributed scoped-store use and mutation/reload need separate qualification.
